name: Customer Sales Deck for a SaaS Product
description: A customer-specific SaaS value proposal in navy, white, and bright orange, translating quantified buyer friction into solution fit, product workflow, proof, ROI, pricing, and a mutual action plan.
style_guide:
# Customer Sales Deck for a SaaS Product

## Purpose

Build a customer-specific enterprise sales story that begins with the buyer's verified priorities and ends with a credible mutual action plan. The narrative connects quantified friction to the solution, product workflow, proof, customer-specific economics, implementation, pricing, and buying milestones. It is not a generic product brochure. All preview names, metrics, prices, dates, testimonials, and account facts are fictional.

## Visual signature

Use strong midnight navy structure, white evidence surfaces, and vivid orange for the proposed value path and calls to action. The cover may use a geometric navy-white split with an orange wedge; body pages remain bright and analytical. Headlines are bold modern sans-serif; mono labels organize account context and commercial metadata. Use flat panels, thin rules, simple flow diagrams, and compact tables rather than screenshots or stock photos.

## Layout

- Fixed 16:9 canvas with `90–110 px` side margins and a 12-column grid.
- Reserve `145–180 px` for eyebrow, buyer-specific conclusion headline, and short support.
- Favor `5/7` context splits, current-to-future mappings, a five-step workflow, proof-plus-ROI split, and implementation-plus-commercial split.
- Use square cards with one-pixel borders and very limited shadow if required for contrast.
- Keep at least 70 percent of ordinary body pages white or cool off-white.

## Colors

- Midnight navy `#081E3A`: cover, titles, headers, current-state structure, and commercial authority.
- Vivid orange `#FF6B1A`: value lever, selected capability, CTA, timeline gate, and buyer decision highlight.
- White `#FFFFFF`: dominant canvas and cards.
- Cool canvas `#F4F7FA`: secondary fields and table stripes.
- Ink `#10213A`: body text.
- Muted slate `#62708A`: explanatory copy.
- Electric blue `#1F6FE5`: links, product flow, and secondary data emphasis.
- Red may mark a verified current pain or risk only; green may mark validated proof only.

## Typography

Use `Inter`, `Aptos`, `Arial`, or `Helvetica Neue`; use `IBM Plex Mono` for account, period, SKU, source, and commercial terms. Cover title `56–70 px`; body conclusion `36–48 px`; KPI `42–58 px`; panel title `20–26 px`; body `13–17 px`; label and source `10–12 px`. Keep numerals tabular in ROI and pricing tables.

## Page archetypes

### 1. Cover, buyer outcome, and commercial summary

Use a navy-white split and one orange geometric accent. Lead with the buyer outcome, not the product name. Include account, buying group, meeting purpose, review date, and only verified high-level economic anchors such as payback or value range.

### 2. Buyer context and quantified friction

Show two or three verified business frictions with baseline, frequency, affected population, economic impact, source, and executive priority. Separate symptoms from root mechanisms. Attribute customer statements or label them as seller synthesis.

### 3. Solution mapping and value levers

Map each friction to one solution behavior and measurable value lever. Use a current-state-to-future-state flow, not a feature catalog. Make integration, process, data, and organizational assumptions visible.

### 4. Product workflow and core capabilities

Show the end-to-end user or system journey in four to six steps. Each step includes user, trigger, action, product capability, output, and handoff. Distinguish available, configurable, planned, and partner-delivered capability. Avoid unreadable UI screenshots.

### 5. Customer proof and ROI model

Pair one or two comparable proof cases with a buyer-specific value model. Identify why each case is comparable, disclose source and period, and do not imply guaranteed outcomes. ROI must show baseline, drivers, adoption ramp, benefit timing, cost, sensitivity, payback, owner, and validation status.

### 6. Implementation, pricing, and mutual action plan

Use one integrated page for phases, responsibilities, commercial option, inclusions and exclusions, dependencies, and buying milestones. Every MAP row has seller owner, customer owner, target date, evidence of completion, and consequence of delay. Pricing must state term, billing basis, units, taxes, implementation, renewal logic, and validity date.

## Commercial integrity

Never invent buyer pain, stakeholder alignment, integrations, legal approval, reference outcomes, discount authority, or procurement timing. Distinguish estimated value from contracted price and forecast from guarantee. Reconcile ROI assumptions with implementation and pricing. Identify customer responsibilities and value-realization dependencies. Keep product availability claims aligned with the approved roadmap and contract language.

## Avoid

Do not use generic category claims, feature walls, fake testimonials, decorative product screenshots, unsupported ROI, ambiguous discounts, or a seller-only close plan. Do not color every card. Do not label a stakeholder champion, decision, or approval without evidence.
